newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airbus to agree restructuring in January - Spiegel.
newsitem.headline: Airbus to agree restructuring in January - Spiegel.

text.p: Partners in the four-country Airbus consortium plan in January to sign a memorandum of understanding to restructure the European aircraft group, news weekly Der Spiegel said on Thursday.

The compromise, to be inked at a supervisory board meeting on January 3, will turn Airbus into a joint-stock company under French law which would be better positioned to compete against Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp, which are merging.

Under the plan, France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Dasa and Spain's Casa would bring part of their production facilities as assets into the new company, Der Spiegel said, quoting unnamed sources.

Dasa would contribute two or three of its five Airbus plants. The partners' plants would be valued by March 1997, by when a new management structure would also be agreed, Der Spiegel said in extracts of a report to be published on Saturday.

The plan represents a compromise between Anglo-German efforts to bring in as many assets as possible into the new Airbus structure, and fears at Aerospatiale that it would be weakened if it gave up too much of its operating facilities.
